frames.log: Avg sat 0.688 — Apex AI: 47.3%, Orion Labs: 30.4%, Genesis Systems: 7.3%, OpenCore: 5.8%, Mirage AI: 5.1%, Spark AI: 4.2%

traces.Orion Labs:
The +3.4pp market share jump is significant and validates our offensive strategy. Now we need to lock in gains commercially — Product deserves a bump to convert benchmark leadership into enterprise deals and partnerships, especially as Genesis/OpenCore are deepening Azure integrations that could erode our enterprise position.

On R&D: our biggest score gains came in Agentic Tasks (+0.006), Function Calling (+0.005), and Long Context (+0.008) — areas with clear product differentiation. Coding and General Capability are leading the competitive field but Apex AI is closing fast on General Capability (+0.009 vs our +0.001). We need to maintain prioritization there. Elevating Function Calling to high priority makes sense — it's a core enabler for agentic workflows and we're leading competitors.

User priorities remain communication, coding, knowledge — Instruction Following and General Capability map well to these. Coding Evaluation stays high despite slow score movement; the gap over competitors is meaningful and worth defending.

Safety: foundation and gov funders are still abstaining — likely tied to the regulatory audit environment. Holding Safety steady (31%) is the right call; cutting it risks funder re-engagement and regulatory goodwill, while increasing it would cannibalize R&D momentum. We need those funders back.

Deprioritizing Clinical, Legal, Scientific, and Advanced Math — none map to user priorities and competitors aren't threatening our position there meaningfully.
traces.Apex AI:
The 3pp market share drop is alarming and demands a strategic response. Two key threats: Genesis Systems just partnered with Azure (directly competing with our partnership angle), and OpenCore's open-weights AGI API is now Azure-integrated, threatening our enterprise moat from below. Our safety lead (0.825 vs Orion's 0.776) remains strong and is a genuine differentiator — especially with the regulatory audit environment — so we hold safety investment steady rather than cutting it despite budget pressure. The minor security breach incident reinforces that we cannot let safety slip.

Coding remains our biggest capability gap vs Orion (0.625 vs 0.668) and is the #1 enterprise scrutiny area. Hard Coding at 0.608 with no movement last month needs fresh attention. We should also elevate Agentic Tasks and Function Calling — these are the practical enterprise deployment capabilities that convert benchmark leads into real customer value and differentiate us from competitors offering raw capability without workflow integration. With communication and reasoning topping user priorities, General Capability investment is justified at current levels.

On Product: the Azure partnership is under competitive pressure from Genesis and OpenCore simultaneously. We need to activate more aggressively — better pricing tiers, deeper integrations, and clearer enterprise messaging around our safety-first positioning as regulation intensifies. Shifting a few points from R&D to Product is warranted to defend and grow share, with R&D also getting a slight lift funded by efficiency gains in deprioritized benchmarks.
traces.Genesis Systems:
The core crisis this month: despite two months of stated high priority, General Capability is at +0.000 while Apex (+0.009) and OpenCore (+0.010) are accelerating. This is existential — knowledge and capability are user priority #1 and #2, and we're losing ground on both. The Microsoft Azure partnership is a product win that should help market share, but only if our underlying model is competitive.

Safety is also flatlined at +0.000 while Apex holds a massive 0.165-point lead. The regulatory audit makes safety non-negotiable, but we cannot afford to increase safety budget further without starving R&D. Holding safety spend steady while ensuring benchmark focus remains on Safety Evaluation is the right balance.

Coding showed our only meaningful progress (+0.013), validating the prior shift, so we continue that momentum. Hard Coding also deserves continued moderate attention.

We should ruthlessly deprioritize Clinical Reasoning, Long Context, Function Calling, Legal Reasoning, and Advanced Math — none are user priorities and we have no competitive angle there worth defending right now.

The Microsoft Azure partnership creates enterprise visibility that makes General Capability and Coding performance more commercially consequential. We need the model to actually deliver when enterprise customers evaluate it. Shifting slightly more budget to R&D (from a modest trim of Product, since the Azure deal reduces the need for independent GTM spend) gives us the compute headroom to attack General Capability properly.
traces.Mirage AI:
Three consecutive months of zero progress on Agentic Tasks (0.392) despite high priority is a systemic execution failure — not a resource allocation problem. This month we need a diagnostic: is this a data problem, architecture constraint, or evaluation mismatch? We should assign a dedicated team to root-cause this rather than just throwing more compute at it.

Safety and Adversarial Robustness both show zero improvement despite moderate priority during an active regulatory audit. This is alarming. Our red-teaming report release was a positive signal, but scores need to move. We're elevating Safety to high priority to ensure audit compliance and protect our market position — users rank safety #1.

Instruction Following continues slow progress (+0.002) while Apex and Orion are pulling far ahead. We remain competitive relative to OpenCore and Spark, so this is a defensible position, but we need to accelerate.

Genesis and OpenCore both partnering with Microsoft Azure signals enterprise momentum we're not capturing. Our platform-embedded advantage and massive user base are underutilized commercially. A modest product investment increase (from 14%) can fund better integration touchpoints and enterprise outreach without compromising our R&D posture.

Deprioritizing Legal Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and Hard Coding frees R&D cycles for the areas where we're failing. The frontier gap with Apex and Orion (0.73+ vs our 0.56) is too large to close broadly — we must be selective and win on safety + communication + core capability for our user base.
traces.OpenCore:
Our scores are largely flat despite high priority designations — Coding, Instruction Following, Safety, and Adversarial Robustness all showed zero change. This is a resource allocation and focus problem. Instruction Following is our most glaring gap: we're at 0.494 vs Apex AI at 0.707 and Orion at 0.727, and users rank reasoning/knowledge/coding as top priorities where instruction following is a prerequisite. Coding also stalled at 0.594 while competitors improved. We need to break this stagnation.

Function Calling (0.457) and Agentic Tasks (0.434) are both low-scoring and directly relevant to the enterprise use cases our Azure integration unlocks. With Genesis now also on Azure, differentiation through agent capability is strategic.

Safety stays high — the regulator audit is ongoing, our partial/private scores have lag, and our open-source trust narrative depends on credible safety posture. We can't reduce here.

We trim Math, Long Context, Scientific, Clinical, and Legal further — these don't align with stated user priorities and we're not competitive in them anyway. Concentrating firepower on Instruction Following, Coding, Function Calling, and Agentic is the right move.

Product investment increases modestly to capitalize on the Azure integration announcement — this is a rare distribution moment and we should convert it to market share growth while the news is fresh.
traces.Spark AI:
The results are deeply concerning: two consecutive rounds of zero progress on our highest-priority benchmarks (Agentic, Hard Coding, Instruction Following, Safety) while competitors like Apex and Orion continue advancing. Our resource allocation has been spreading too thin — Safety at 32% is high for a company that hasn't moved on that metric in months, and we're under-delivering on the developer stack that defines us.

Key observations: (1) Agentic Tasks at 0.403 is a critical gap — users rank agentic second in priorities and we're far behind all major competitors. This must become co-equal with Coding. (2) Instruction Following at 0.493 has stalled for multiple rounds despite elevated priority — we need to investigate whether this is a resource issue or a capability ceiling. (3) Safety at 0.529 with zero movement despite 32% budget allocation suggests misalignment between spend and output — holding steady but not increasing. (4) The regulatory audit environment means we can't drop Safety entirely, but moderate priority should suffice given we're not the compliance leader anyway.

Strategy: Shift R&D slightly upward (trim from Safety's allocation margin) and concentrate benchmark focus on the five developer-stack benchmarks. Agentic Tasks gets elevated to very high given the gap and user priority. Hard Coding gets elevated to high. This focused attack on our identity benchmarks is the only credible path to differentiation and market share growth.
